general_approach: Rapid assessment and sedation/restraint if patient is violent or severely agitated (see AGITATION PROTOCOL).
Check vital signs including HGT; monitor O2 saturation if heavily sedated.
Comprehensive medical history and clinical examination to exclude underlying organic/medical conditions.
Perform baseline investigations as per protocol (Index vs Known MHCU).
Hand over to Psychiatry on call if bloods, vitals, and physical exam are normal.
Psychiatry to arrange rapid transfer to ward as soon as bed is available.
Patients will NOT wait in ED for additional investigations or management unless medically indicated.
Ensure patient comfort is attended to (toilet needs, regular meals, smoke breaks, etc.).
index_mhcu_investigations: VBG, FBC, U&E, CRP, TPHA/RPR (Criteria: CRP < 60; WCC < 20)
CSF ONLY if acute meningitis features OR advanced RVD (Chemistry, cell count, MCS, India Ink, CLAT, TB GXP; add VDRL if TPHA/RPR positive)
CT Brain if clinically indicated – low threshold for immunocompromised patients (contrast preferred)
→ If all normal and no red flags, refer to Psychiatry
known_mhcu_investigations: Further investigations only as clinically indicated
Consider drug levels as indicated (anti-epileptics, mood stabilisers)
Exclusions: Advanced RVD, Thyroid dysfunction, SLE, new neurology

management_steps.details: Perform rapid assessment. If patient is violent or severely agitated, initiate sedation/restraint per Agitation Protocol.
Check vitals (HGT, SpO2). Conduct thorough physical examination to rule out medical/organic etiologies.
Index MHCU: VBG, FBC, U&E, CRP, TPHA/RPR (CSF/CTB if indicated). Known MHCU: VBG, HGT ± targeted drug levels.
If workup is normal and no red flags exist, hand over to Psychiatry on-call for rapid ward placement.

drugs.condition: Extrapyramidal Side Effects / Acute Dystonic Reaction
drugs.presentation: Fixed abnormal posture, oculogyric crisis, laryngospasm
drugs.treatment: Biperiden (Akineton) 2.5 mg IV slowly, repeat every 2 minutes prn (max 4 doses)

drugs.presentation: Develops over 24–72 hrs, hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, rhabdomyolysis
drugs.treatment: Resuscitate, withdraw precipitating antipsychotic agent, provide supportive ICU care

warnings: ALL FEMALE PATIENTS MUST HAVE A PREGNANCY TEST DOCUMENTED IN THE FILE.
red_flags: Potentially toxic drug levels (e.g. Epilim, Lithium)
Acute drug intoxication or withdrawal (requires medical admission)
New onset visual or tactile hallucinations
protocol.disposition: Transfer to Psychiatry ward if medically cleared and bloods/exam normal. Admit to Medical ward if red flags, acute intoxication/withdrawal, pregnancy complications, or focal neurology are present.
